title: Beta Blockers: Receptor Selectivity and Contraindications
subject: Pharmacology
preview: Beta-1 receptors influence heart rate and contractility; beta-2 receptors influence bronchial and vascular smooth muscle.
quickRevision: Beta-1 receptors influence heart rate and contractility; beta-2 receptors influence bronchial and vascular smooth muscle.
Nonselective beta blockade can precipitate bronchospasm in susceptible patients.
Indications and risks vary in heart failure, ischemic heart disease, arrhythmia and pregnancy.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Beta-1 receptors influence heart rate and contractility; beta-2 receptors influence bronchial and vascular smooth muscle.
Cardioselective beta blockers preferentially block beta-1 at usual doses but selectivity is incomplete and dose-dependent.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Nonselective beta blockade can precipitate bronchospasm in susceptible patients.
Indications and risks vary in heart failure, ischemic heart disease, arrhythmia and pregnancy.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not abruptly stop long-term beta blockers without a plan because rebound sympathetic effects can occur.
